translationRepairs: Yelu Xidi was descended from the Prince of Chu on his mother's side.
Yelu Xidi was a descendant of the Prince of Chu of the Mengfu lineage.
孟父楚國王之後 names the Mengfu (eldest-uncle) Yelu lineage, not maternal descent; the proposed fix is right in substance, but the parenthetical '(Meng Father)' is awkward in idiomatic English.
Yelu Xidi was a descendant of the Prince of Chu on his mother's side.
Yelu Xidi was a descendant of the Prince of Chu of the Mengfu lineage.
孟父 is the Mengfu lineage label, not 'mother's side'; the proposed 'Prince of Chu of the Mengfu lineage' restores the correct sense of 孟父楚國王之後.
The empress dowager agreed and added the titles Golden Purple Glory Grandee and Inspector Grand Preceptor.
The empress dowager agreed and added the titles Golden Purple Glory Grandee and Inspector Grand Commandant.
檢校太尉 is Inspector Grand Commandant; 太尉 is not Grand Preceptor (太傅), so the proposed title is the accurate repair.
The empress dowager followed this and added the titles Golden Purple Glory Grandee and Grand Preceptor on inspection.
The empress dowager followed this and added the titles Golden Purple Glory Grandee and Inspector Grand Commandant.
檢校太尉 means Inspector Grand Commandant; rendering 太尉 as Grand Preceptor and 'on inspection' misreads both 太尉 and 檢校.
He answered, "Each morning I recite the precepts left by Taizu, Taizong, and my forebears; I have had no time for Buddhism."
He answered, "Each morning I recite the precepts left by Taizu, Taizong, and my late forebear; I have had no time for Buddhism."
先臣 is singular for the speaker's late father/forebear-minister, not plural 'forebears'; 'my late forebear' matches 先臣遺訓.
Yelu Xuegu, whose courtesy name was Yixin, was a grandson by a concubine of the Yuyue Wa.
Yelu Xuegu, whose courtesy name was Yixinyin, was a grandson by a concubine of the Yuyue Wa.
字乙辛隱 is the three-character courtesy name Yixinyin; 'Yixin' omits 隱 and is incomplete.
